steps.title: Prepare 1.5 M sucrose solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 20.538 g sucrose (Sigma 84097) in water, adjust volume to 40 mL, filter, store at 4 °C indefinitely; for long‑term storage aliquot and keep at –20 °C. If white bacterial growth appears at 4 °C, discard and use a fresh unopened aliquot.

steps.title: Make Nuclei Isolation Medium 1
steps.instruction: Combine 6.2625 mL water, 7.5 mL 1.5 M sucrose (final 250 mM, 8.56 % w/v), 562.5 µL 2 M KCl (final 25 mM), 450 µL 1 M HEPES pH 7.5 (final 10 mM), and 225 µL 1 M MgCl₂ (final 5 mM) to a total volume of 45 mL. Vortex to mix and store at 4 °C indefinitely.

steps.title: Prepare 10 % Igepal solution (optional)
steps.instruction: Mix 900 µL water with 100 µL Igepal CA‑630 (Sigma I8896) to a final volume of 1 mL (10 % v/v). Vortex and store at 18 °C–27 °C indefinitely.

steps.title: Prepare 1 mM DTT solution
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL 1 M DTT (Sigma 646563) to 1 mL water, vortex to mix, yielding 1 mM DTT; store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Nuclei Isolation Buffer without Triton
steps.instruction: To 6 mL Nuclei Isolation Medium 1 add 6 µL 1 mM DTT (final 1 µM DTT). Vortex and keep on ice.

steps.title: Prepare Nuclei Isolation Buffer with Triton
steps.instruction: To 2 mL Nuclei Isolation Buffer without Triton add 20 µL 10 % Triton X‑100 (Sigma 93443) to obtain a final Triton concentration of 0.1 % (v/v). Vortex and keep on ice.

substeps.instruction: Chill a 2 mL Dounce homogenizer (Sigma D8938) on ice; for >200 mg tissue use a larger homogenizer (D9063 for 7 mL, D9938 for 15 mL, D9188 for 40 mL, D0189 for 100 mL) and scale the reaction accordingly.
Add 2 mL ice‑cold Nuclei Isolation Buffer with Triton to the homogenizer.
Add up to 200 mg tissue.
Dounce the tissue with 5 strokes of the loose pestle (A) followed by 15 strokes of the tight pestle (B).
Transfer the homogenate to a conical tube.
Centrifuge at 100 g for 8 min at 4 °C.
Carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the soft pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 2 mL Nuclei Isolation Buffer without Triton.
Centrifuge again at 100 g for 8 min at 4 °C.
Remove the supernatant carefully.
Resuspend the pellet in a second 2 mL of Nuclei Isolation Buffer without Triton.
Filter the suspension through a 40‑µm cell strainer (Corning 352340) or alternative sizes (35 µm 352235, 100 µm 352360).
Keep the nuclei on ice until fixation.

steps.title: Purify and size‑select libraries
steps.instruction: Purify PCR products and perform size selection, avoiding cross‑contamination of liquids between plates that use overlapping indices.

substeps.instruction: Pool all wells from a 96‑well plate (total volume ≈2.4 mL).
Add DNA Binding Buffer (Zymo D4004‑1‑L) at a 1:5 ratio (PCR : buffer) to reach 12 mL buffer; vortex (total volume ≈14.4 mL).
Load the mixture onto six Zymo PCR purification columns (D4013), loading each column three times (≈800 µL per load).
Wash columns according to the manufacturer’s protocol and elute each column into 66.7 µL TE (ThermoFisher AM9849); pool eluates to obtain 400 µL total library.
Optional control: for each positive/negative control well (25 µL), mix with 125 µL DNA Binding Buffer and elute into 6 µL TE.
Pause point – store purified libraries at –20 °C.
Measure DNA concentration with a Qubit 1× dsDNA HS assay and fragment size with a Bioanalyzer High Sensitivity DNA kit (or Fragment Analyzer).
Take half of the library (~200 µL) and add SPRIselect beads at 0.7 X (140 µL) or 0.6 X (120 µL) ratio; incubate, place on magnet, discard supernatant, wash, and elute into 50 µL TE.
Retain the remaining half (~200 µL) as a backup.
Pause point – store final libraries at –20 °C.
Measure DNA concentration and fragment size again with Qubit and Bioanalyzer.

steps.title: Sequence libraries and analyze data
steps.instruction: Generate sequencing data and process with the dip‑c pipeline.

substeps.instruction: Sequence libraries on an Illumina platform (HiSeq or NovaSeq) with paired‑end 150‑bp reads and dual 8‑bp indices; aim for 3–6 million read pairs per cell.
If diploid reconstruction is not required, use paired‑end 75‑bp reads.
Optional shallow test: sequence ≈1,000 reads per plate on a MiSeq to assess contact rate before deep sequencing.
Analyze raw data with the dip‑c software (https://github.com/tanlongzhi/dip-c).

description: The protocol below describes the application of diploid chromatin conformation capture (Dip-C) to single nuclei isolated from the human (fresh frozen postmortem) or mouse brain. Procedures include the isolation and fixation of nuclei from tissues, chromatin conformation capture (3C/Hi-C), flow-sorting and lysis of single nuclei, whole-genome amplification (WGA) with Nextera, and DNA sequencing. If whole cells instead of nuclei are used, please follow the Optional instructions throughout the protocol for steps to add and to skip. Although Dip-C is a single-cell assay, the chromatin conformation capture (3C/Hi-C) step is performed in bulk—typically on 500 k–1 m cells or nuclei. There is no lower bound on the number of cells or nuclei in principle. Users have reported success with as few as 50 cells; similar procedures have been demonstrated on as few as 1 cell (Flyamer et al., 2017; Stevens et al., 2017). For low cell numbers, the 3C/Hi-C reaction may be scaled down (fewer cells would consume less enzymes); alternative versions that do not involve centrifugation between digestion and ligation (e.g., Rao et al., 2014 or the Arima-SC kit) may further help to minimize cell loss. If many chromatin contacts per cell are preferred, multiplex end-tagging amplification (META) (Xing et al., 2021) can be used in place of Nextera for whole-genome amplification (WGA). META detects 2 times as many contacts per cell as Nextera. Please refer to Tan et al. (2018) for detailed procedures. Note that META requires additional considerations: (a) META involves custom Tn5 transposomes and 2 additional primer removal and PCR steps. (b) During Illumina sequencing, the first 39 bp of Read 1 and of Read 2 are META transposon DNA, effectively truncating the (usable) read length. In addition, these bps have low diversity, requiring pooling with a non-META library (e.g., 20% Phi-X).
